title: Funeral marches and why jazz is harder to play
summary: Old funeral marches differ from today's; he says slow dirges are easy to play while the return jazz is harder because of faster execution.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Can you remember anything about the funerals when you were a boy? Did they march just like they do today? Have the same kind of funeral marches in the brass bands when you were a boy? Same kind? Yeah. When your father played, what kind of music did they use?

They played some of the same things, but I don't hear some of the funeral marches that they used to play. They'll be different ones. Yeah. But they still play some, but I don't play some of the funeral marches that they did here.
Were they difficult to play? Tense?
Who?
Were they hard to play? Fuel marches? Yeah.
No. Ain't no funeral at all that's hard to march. Marches easy.
No, I mean to play. To play.
Huh?
I mean to play the part.
You say they're hard.
Are they hard to play?
Hard to what? The funeral marches? Yeah. No. Ain't no funeral marches hard. It's easy. That's slow music.
Full time, you know?
Yeah. That's slow music. It's no, you just walk, walk and you're playing, you're playing slow parts. That's easy.
How about when you're coming back? Huh? How about when you're coming back?
It's harder.
It's harder.
It's harder. Jazz is harder than common times.
Why is that?
Huh?
Why? Why is it hard?
It's slow music. It's slow. Jazz is faster. You're playing jazz. You're executing. You're executing faster.
You're going to think what you're playing? Huh? You're going to think faster.
Well, yeah. Well, yeah. Yeah. You're going to think with these. It's already in your brains already.
But you just said faster execution. Huh? Faster execution, though.
